author: Rick Gogreve
title: Jefferson Parish Council's tennis plan for playground faces opposition - NewsBreak
text:
By Rick Gogreve ,
1 hours ago METAIRIE, La. ( WGNO ) — The Jefferson Parish Council has agreed in principle to collaborate with a private company to put a tennis complex where the Johnny Bright Playground is now.
In a “letter of intent” signed by all the council except Jennifer Van Vranken the company has six months to find $16 million to fund the project.
However, Councilman Hans Liljeberg says the agreement is completely preliminary and something the council can back out of at any time.
“It’s nothing we can’t walk back. If there’s opposition, I mean look, I’ve been wrong before a lot,” Liljeberg said.
Boil water advisory declared in Hammond In fact, there is opposition.
“It’s really hard when you have people that you’ve elected that are supposed to look out for you that blindside you and then come back and say and then come back and say that everybody knew about it. It’s just very disheartening,” Johnny Bright Playground Booster Executive Board Member Jacques Legrand said.
Councilman Scott Walker says the playground just isn’t used that much.
“We have too many playgrounds in Jefferson parish. JPRD can’t manage all of these playgrounds with the budget that they have, and some playgrounds don’t get the same participation in some cases and Johnny bright is one of those,” Walker said.
Some disagree, highlighting just the track and field program alone.
“We had over 100 kids compete in our track program that just finished, and we won the highest rated teams on the east bank and west bank,” Legrand said.
Some parents say if they lose the playground, it will be like losing a home away from home.
“My children have met so many friends, and it really feels like a family,” playground parent Courtney Brown said.
